From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP and sprint commitments — initial draft

Hi Lucy,

Thanks again for carving out time earlier. Attached is a lightweight Mutual Action Plan we usually use to align evaluation scope, responsibilities, and a close sprint. I pasted the key milestones below so it's easy to skim.

Quick asks from our side:
- Can you confirm the internal stakeholders we should include (legal, procurement, infra)?
- Are you comfortable with a target close week of the week of Mar 23?
- Can procurement commit to a two-week review once contract language is shared?

High-level milestones (proposed):
1) Kickoff & environment access (week of Feb 22)
2) Eval run & success criteria validation (Mar 1–12)
3) Stakeholder review & procurement (Mar 15–19)
4) Final sign & deployment plan (Mar 23–27)

Link to MAP (editable): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MAPdummy-BSA
Attachments: Redwood_MAP_Template_v1.gdoc, MAP_Sprint_Checklist.pdf

If you confirm the timeline by EOD Tue we'll lock calendar invites and assign owners for the sprint tasks.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Sr. Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

From: Lucy Park <lucy@blueshift.ai>

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP and sprint commitments — initial draft

Thanks, Soojin — this is a helpful template. A few things from our side before we lock dates: 

- Evaluation environment: we'll need a day of VPN access + a short runbook for temporary creds and expected data flows. Can you include a step for that in the MAP?
- SSO: our identity team prefers SAML-based SSO; what's Redwood's typical lead time to enable SAML?
- Procurement: I'm looping procurement (Maya Chen) into the thread — they will want SOC2 evidence and standard T&Cs.

I've attached our RFP and a proposed internal timeline. Overall the proposed close week looks doable but procurement may shift a week depending on redlines.

Proposed internal milestone adjustments:
- Kickoff: Feb 22 (preferred)
- Eval window: Mar 1–10
- Procurement review: Mar 11–19

I'll introduce Maya directly in my next reply.

Best,
Lucy Park
Director of Data Products | BlueShift Analytics
lucy@blueshift.ai

Attachments: BlueShift_RFP_v1.pdf

Soojin / Aditya — quick internal note and suggested edits to the shared MAP (I made inline comments in the doc). High-level suggestions: 

1) Add an "Environment access" milestone with owner assignment:
   - Infra handoff (Marcus Lin) — provisioning test nodes + VPN (due Feb 21)
   - Temporary creds + runbook (Aditya Rao) — due Feb 23

2) Add a "Canary eval" submilestone during the eval window so we validate latency/cost on representative traffic.

3) Procurement stream — add a contract share milestone and a 5-business-day review expectation (to keep things tight). Legal should be ready to jump on redlines as soon as procurement confirms scope.

I attached a quick assignments table to map owners to deliverables. I also flagged the SOC2 summary page in our security pack so we can send that to Maya.

Action items:
- Aditya: draft the temp-creds runbook and post to the MAP (due Feb 18)
- Marcus: confirm node counts and estimated token throughput (due Feb 19)
- Soojin: confirm kickoff time with Lucy and include procurement contact in invites (ASAP)

Thanks — I think tightening owners will make the timeline credible.

Marissa
Senior Customer Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_Assignments_table.xlsx, Security_Pack_SOC2_summary.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Updated MAP + environment access plan

Hi Lucy — thanks for the quick turnaround and for attaching the RFP. I updated the MAP with Marissa's owner assignments and added a short environment access plan you can follow when we spin up test nodes. Highlights below and the editable doc is linked.

Environment access (summary):
- Infra provisioning: Redwood will pre-provision two test nodes for the canary evaluation. Marcus will confirm exact specs by Feb 19.
- Temporary creds: Aditya will circulate one-day scoped creds and a runbook for ingestion/metrics by Feb 18.
- SSO/SAML: Redwood supports SAML; typical enablement time is 7–10 business days after the identity team completes the metadata exchange.
- Security artifacts: sending SOC2 summary and our standard DPA (see attachments).

Link to updated MAP: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MAPdummy-BSA (you should have edit/comment access)
Related hubspot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/49321
Attachments now shared: Security_Pack_SOC2_summary.pdf

Next steps:
- Confirm kickoff on Feb 22 (proposed time range: 09:00–11:00 PT)
- Aditya to post temp-creds runbook by Feb 18
- Marcus to confirm node specs by Feb 19

If that all looks reasonable let me know and I'll send the calendar invites and include procurement.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Soojin
Sr. Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Updated MAP + environment access plan

Thanks, Soojin — that works for us.

Maya (procurement) — I'm forwarding the RFP and the MAP to you so you can confirm internal timing. Our preferred kickoff is Feb 22 at 10:00 PT; if that still works let us lock it.

We reviewed the SOC2 summary and it looks fine as a first pass. Procurement will follow up if they need anything else; I'll ask them to do the 5-business-day review you suggested.

Confirmed next steps from BlueShift:
- Confirm kickoff (we accept Feb 22, 10:00 PT)
- Procurement to review RFP and SOC2 (Maya will own)
- Internal infra to prepare sample dataset for the canary eval (ops will share by Feb 19)

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Lucy Park
